hypothesis: Does historical study-level CV-of-CVs contain prospective information about subsequent insect abundance deterioration, beyond the conventional Round 1 baseline?

predictor.name: C_g
predictor.constituent_definition: CV_i = sample SD / mean of raw Number over a constituent series' own usable years within the study's frozen 10-year historical window (>=2 usable years required)
predictor.zero_mean_handling: CV_i undefined (None), series excluded from constituent set for that window

inferential_unit: (DataSource_ID, one fixed 10-year historical window) pair; C_g broadcast to each outcome-contributing constituent series, analyzed with DataSource_ID clustering -- never plot- or series-level as the independent replication unit
effective_n_definition: number of adequate (study, window) units meeting the adequacy gate below (expected ~19-20), NOT the number of constituent series or plots
historical_window_definition: first 10 elements of the sorted, deduplicated union of usable years across all of a study's Round-1-eligible series (rank-based, not calendar-year arithmetic)
chronology_design_definition: fixed 10-year history window (study's own first 10 union-years) then a fully held-out later period (all remaining union-years); non-overlapping, deterministic, no window search

future_outcome.formula: OLS slope of log1p(Number) on Year over a constituent series' own Round-1 late window
future_outcome.h4_specific_eligibility_filter: series.late_year_min > max(study.hist_years) -- i.e. that series' Round-1 late window must fall entirely after the study's H4 historical cutoff

predicted_direction.interpretation: lower (tighter) historical C_g predicts a worse (more negative) future abundance trend; higher C_g predicts a better (less negative) trend
predicted_direction.derivation: direct analogy to Round 1's frozen H1_DIRECTION=+1 convention for D3/1, D4/1, Q90/50, applied one level up to C_g; derived from the original manuscript's motivating theory only, never from inspecting real outcome data

model_spec.type: ordinary least squares, standardized features (fit within training fold only)
model_spec.fallback: Ridge, alpha=1.0, triggered if training design matrix condition number > 1e8

primary_statistic.name: delta_rmse
primary_statistic.formula: RMSE(M0) - RMSE(M1), pooled out-of-fold across LOSO folds
primary_statistic.sign_convention: positive = improvement from adding C_g (identical to Round 1)

secondary_statistic.name: C_g_coefficient
secondary_statistic.formula: standardized OLS coefficient on C_g in the full-sample M1 fit
secondary_statistic.note: secondary only; cannot rescue a failed primary result

permutation_procedure.scheme: between-study permutation of the study-to-C_g mapping across H4-eligible studies; outcome, baseline features, and study membership held fixed
permutation_procedure.exchangeability_restriction: permute only among the H4-eligible study set; never mixed with Round 1's series-level NC1/NC2
permutation_procedure.tie_handling: included in the >= comparison, no separate rule

support_rule.NOT_SUPPORTED: primary permutation p > 0.05, regardless of delta_rmse sign; OR delta_rmse <= 0 regardless of p
support_rule.DIRECTIONALLY_OPPOSITE: primary permutation test rejects the null against the predicted direction (delta_rmse reliably negative)
support_rule.UNINTERPRETABLE_BLOCKED: fewer than 10 H4-eligible studies survive every gate

stop_rule: After H4 is executed: no alternate constituent-series thresholds, historical windows, chronological splits, robust CV variants, transformations, study removals, future outcomes, aggregations, subgroup searches, CHANGE hypothesis, permutation-count increases, or alternative model families. If H4 fails, the primary conclusion is that historical LEVEL CV-of-CVs, as prospectively defined, is not supported as an early-warning indicator in these data -- no weaker or requalified restatement is permitted without a wholly new, independently-frozen protocol.
